build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 13: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 16's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 4-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 13's value table (side 1's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 13's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$003F, channel 0's script at +$000E and 0 for channels 1, 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 16 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 10, frame 1 then 3, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 1, frame 3 then 3, frame 4 then 12, frame 1 then 5, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 1, frame 6 then 1, frame 7 then 3, frame 8 then 1, frame 9 then 8, frame 10 then 1, frame 2 then 1. One pass takes 53 steps.

Picture 13's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 31 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 10 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 5 and 16: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 2 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 6 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 11 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 9: a run count of 0 to start, then 13 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 33 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 10 and 11: a run count of 0 to start, then 9 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 23 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 12: a run count of 0 to start, then 11 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 28 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 13: a run count of 0 to start, then 13 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 36 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 9 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 14: a run count of 0 to start, then 12 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 28 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 10 of picture 13, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 15: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 13's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,196th byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
